title: Polynomial-time unary encoding of a configuration length
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let $d,c$ be natural numbers. For each bit string $y$, form its decoded first component $x$ (taking the empty string when decoding fails). The function that outputs a unary string of length $V_{N,d,c}(|x|)$ is polynomial-time computable, where $V_{N,d,c}(n)=W_N(4d(n+1)^c+1)+|\operatorname{bits}(n+1)|+1$ and $W_N=|H_N|+3k_N+1$; here $k_N$ is the number of work tapes, $H_N$ is the finite set of state-and-output-summary pairs, and $\operatorname{bits}(m)$ is the binary digit list of $m$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet.
